newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: YACHTING-AUSTRALIA LAUNCHES SEARCH FOR FRENCH YACHTSMAN.
newsitem.headline: YACHTING-AUSTRALIA LAUNCHES SEARCH FOR FRENCH YACHTSMAN.

text.p: An Australian air force Orion plane left on Thursday to search for French yachtsman Raphael Dinelli after distress signals from his yacht were picked up, a maritime rescue official said.

Australian Maritime Safety Authority (AMSA) spokesman David Gray told reporters three of four distress beacons aboard Dinelli's 18.3 metre (60 ft) yacht Algimouss had been set off early on Thursday morning as the yacht encountered winds of up to 40 knots and heavy seas.
"The yacht is not in voice communication...so we have no idea of the distress situatioon on board as yet," Gray said.
The Orion left its base in South Australia state at about 4.30 p.m. (0530 GMT) and would take about four hours to fly the 1,200 nautical miles to the search zone southwest of Western Australia.
The plane was carrying liferafts, food and communication equipment to drop to Dinelli, 28, who is competing in the Vendee Globe solo round-the-world race.
Dinelli's distress signals were picked up in France, where race officials use a different international satellite navigation system to that used in Australia.
"The French (maritime officials) immediately requested assistance from Australia, whose search and rescue responsibility area covers the yacht's present position," Gray said.
"The race organiser has advised that other competing yachts have been alerted and will head towards Dinelli's yacht, but they are not expected to arrive before the aircraft," he said.
Two years ago Australian officials launched a A$1 million (US$790,000) rescue mission to save French yachtswoman Isabelle Autissier, whose yacht was damaged after being rolled in a similar race.
Autissier was eventually winched from her dismasted yacht in an operation criticised by Australian newspapers because Australia and not race officials had to foot the bill.
The other 13 Vendee sailors, including Autissier, were spread out between South Africa and New Zealand.
